question.problem: A supplier of clothing materials looks for flaws before selling the material to customers. On average, there have been $1.7$ flaws per meter. What is the probability of finding fewer than $4$  flaws in the next meter length of the material? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places. You may assume that flaws appear independently and at a constant average rate.
question.worked_solution:
A Poisson random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\lambda }^{x}{e}^{-\lambda }}{x!}
$$

Let $X$ be the number of flaws in a meter length of the material. Since the average rate is $1.7$ flaws per meter, and events occur independently and at a constant average rate, the number of flaws can be modeled as a Poisson random variable with rate $\lambda =1.7,$ and we can write $X∼\text{Po}(1.7).$

So, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{1.7}^{x}{e}^{-1.7}}{x!}
$$

Therefore, the probability of finding fewer than $4$  flaws in the next meter length of the material is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<4) & =P(X\in \{0,1,2,3\}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1)+f(2)+f(3) \\  & =\frac{{1.7}^{0}{e}^{-1.7}}{0!}+\frac{{1.7}^{1}{e}^{-1.7}}{1!}+\frac{{1.7}^{2}{e}^{-1.7}}{2!}+\frac{{1.7}^{3}{e}^{-1.7}}{3!} \\  & ≈0.907\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
